Question B-005-005-011.

Why the correct answer is right: At the source end of a parallel circuit, the branch currents join back together. The source current is the sum of the separate branch currents.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "source voltage divided by the value of one of the resistive elements": That finds only one branch current when that branch resistance is known. It omits the other branches.
- sourceIndex 2: "source voltage divided by the sum of the resistive elements": Dividing by a simple sum treats the resistors as series parts, not parallel branches.
- sourceIndex 3: "current in any one of the parallel branches": One branch current is only part of the source current unless there is only one branch.
